lesson.text: Quick memory: which direction is opposite east? (West.) On a map, east is along to the right and north is up. Grid references use both.
Many maps are covered with a grid of squares. Each square has a name, so you can tell someone exactly where to look.
On simple maps, the columns have letters and the rows have numbers. Read along first, then up: the well is in column B and row 3, so its square is B3.
A saying to remember the order: along the corridor, then up the stairs. Along the bottom first, then up the side.
Bigger maps use numbers both ways: a four-figure grid reference. The first two figures give the column, the last two the row. The mill is in column 14, row 36: square 1436.
On a real map, the numbers are printed on the grid lines. A square takes the numbers of the lines at its bottom-left corner. The numbers get bigger going east and going north.
Try it in the world: lay out a grid of paths 5 squares by 5, with numbered signs along the bottom and up the side. Hide a treasure chest and give a friend its grid reference!

exercises.prompt: Which do you read first in a grid reference?
exercises.hint: Along the corridor, then up the stairs.
exercises.explain: Read along first (the column), then up (the row).

exercises.prompt: Look at the map. Which square is the farm in?
exercises.hint: Find the farm. Go down to read its column letter, then across to read its row number.
exercises.explain: The farm is in column C and row 2, so its square is C2.

exercises.prompt: In the square B3, B is the column and 3 is the row.
exercises.hint: Letters are along the bottom or top; numbers are up the side.
exercises.explain: True: B is the column (along) and 3 is the row (up).

exercises.prompt: What does 'along the corridor, then up the stairs' help you remember?
exercises.hint: It is about the order of a grid reference.
exercises.explain: It reminds you to read along the bottom first, then up the side.

exercises.prompt: Look at the map. What is in square A1?
exercises.hint: Find column A along the top, then row 1 up the side.
exercises.explain: Column A and row 1 meet at the pond.

exercises.prompt: In the grid reference 2547, which figures give the column?
exercises.hint: The first two figures are along the corridor.
exercises.explain: The first two figures, 25, give the column; the last two, 47, give the row.

exercises.prompt: The grid reference 1436 means column 14 and row 36.
exercises.hint: Split the four figures into two pairs.
exercises.explain: True: 14 is the column (along) and 36 is the row (up).

exercises.prompt: Look at the map. What is in square 1537?
exercises.hint: Find column 15 along the top, then row 37 up the side.
exercises.explain: Column 15 and row 37 meet at the barn.

exercises.hint: Which pair is the column in each one?
exercises.explain: False: 4725 is column 47, row 25, but 2547 is column 25, row 47: different squares.

exercises.prompt: On a real map, which corner of a square gives its grid reference?
exercises.hint: The numbers are on the lines. Which lines are along the bottom and up the left?
exercises.explain: A square takes the numbers of the lines at its bottom-left corner.

exercises.prompt: The pond is in square 3162. Tilly walks one square east. Which square is she in now?
exercises.hint: Going east changes the first two figures, the column. Do they go up or down?
exercises.explain: Going east, the column goes up by one: 31 becomes 32, so she is in 3262.

exercises.prompt: Bram is in square 2044 and walks one square north. Which square is he in now?
exercises.hint: Going north changes the last two figures, the row.
exercises.explain: Going north, the row goes up by one: 44 becomes 45, so he is in 2045.

exercises.prompt: On a map, the numbers along the bottom get bigger as you go east.
exercises.hint: East is to the right. Which way do the numbers count?
exercises.explain: True: the numbers get bigger going east (along) and going north (up).

exercises.prompt: Put the steps for finding square 2347 in order.
exercises.hint: Along the corridor first, then up the stairs.
items: look in the square where they meet
exercises.explain: Find 23 along the bottom, go up that column, find 47 up the side, and look where they meet.

exercises.prompt: Look at the map. Match each place to its square.
exercises.hint: Along the bottom first for the letter, then up the side for the number.
exercises.explain: The trees are in C4, the house in B3, the mill in C2 and the rocks in A1.

exercises.prompt: The grid reference is 3862. Which column is the square in?
exercises.hint: The first two figures are along the bottom.
exercises.explain: 38 is the column; 62 is the row.

exercises.prompt: The grid reference is 3862. Which row is the square in?
exercises.hint: The last two figures are up the side.
exercises.explain: 62 is the row; 38 is the column.

exercises.prompt: Sort the grid references: is 31 the column or the row?
exercises.hint: The first two figures give the column, the last two give the row.
exercises.explain: Column 31: 3162 and 3105 start with 31. Row 31: 6231 and 0531 end with 31.

exercises.prompt: Bram starts in square 2044. Match each walk to the square he ends in.
exercises.hint: East and west change the column (the first two figures). North and south change the row.
exercises.explain: East adds 1 to the column: 2144. North adds 1 to the row: 2045. 2 east and 1 north: 22 and 45, so 2245. 1 west and 1 south: 19 and 43, so 1943.
